title_en: Regulations on the Supervision and Management of Safety of Civil Nuclear Facilities of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of ensuring safety in the construction and operation of civil nuclear facilities, safeguarding the health of workers and the public, protecting the environment, and promoting the smooth development of nuclear energy.

Article 3 The siting, design, construction, operation and decommissioning of civil nuclear facilities must implement the policy of safety first; there must be adequate measures to ensure quality, ensure safe operation, prevent nuclear accidents, and limit possible harmful effects; it must be ensured that workers, the public and the environment are not subjected to radiation exposure and contamination exceeding the limits prescribed by the State, and that radiation exposure and contamination are reduced to as low a level as is reasonably achievable.

Article 5 The National Nuclear Safety Administration may establish representative offices in areas where nuclear facilities are concentrated to carry out safety supervision.
The National Nuclear Safety Administration may organize a Nuclear Safety Expert Committee. The Committee shall assist in formulating nuclear safety regulations and nuclear safety technology development plans, and participate in nuclear safety review, assessment, supervision and other work.

Article 9 Before construction of a nuclear facility, the nuclear facility operating entity must submit a "Nuclear Facility Construction Application", a "Preliminary Safety Analysis Report" and other relevant materials to the National Nuclear Safety Administration, and may commence construction only after review and approval and obtaining a "Nuclear Facility Construction Permit".
The construction of a nuclear facility must comply with the conditions specified in the "Nuclear Facility Construction Permit".

Article 10 Before operation of a nuclear facility, the nuclear facility operating entity must submit a "Nuclear Facility Operation Application", a "Final Safety Analysis Report" and other relevant materials to the National Nuclear Safety Administration, and may begin loading nuclear fuel (or feeding material) and commence start-up and commissioning only after review and approval and obtaining the approval document permitting loading (or feeding) and commissioning; it may formally operate only after obtaining a "Nuclear Facility Operation Permit".
The operation of a nuclear facility must comply with the conditions specified in the "Nuclear Facility Operation Permit".

Article 11 In the process of examining and approving the nuclear facility construction application and operation application, the National Nuclear Safety Administration shall consult the relevant departments of the State Council and the people's governments of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the nuclear facility is located. The relevant departments of the State Council and the local people's government shall give a reply within three months.

Article 13 Nuclear facility operator licenses shall be divided into "Operator License" and "Senior Operator License".
Only persons holding an "Operator License" may serve as operators of nuclear facility control systems.
Only persons holding a "Senior Operator License" may serve as operators or supervisors of others operating nuclear facility control systems.
Article 15 The relocation, transfer or decommissioning of a nuclear facility must be applied to the National Nuclear Safety Administration, and may be carried out only after review and approval.

Article 17 When performing their duties, nuclear safety supervisors, by virtue of their certificates, shall have the right to enter the sites of nuclear facility manufacturing, construction and operation, investigate conditions, and collect relevant nuclear safety data.

Article 18 The National Nuclear Safety Administration shall have the right, when necessary, to take compulsory measures to order the nuclear facility operating entity to adopt safety measures or to stop activities that endanger safety.

Article 19 The nuclear facility operating entity shall have the right to refuse any requirements harmful to safety, but must implement the compulsory measures of the National Nuclear Safety Administration.

Article 20 The National Nuclear Safety Administration or the competent department of nuclear facilities shall give appropriate rewards to units and individuals that have made remarkable achievements and contributions in ensuring the safety of nuclear facilities.

Article 22 If a party is dissatisfied with an administrative penalty, it may file a prosecution with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the penalty notice. However, the decision to revoke a nuclear safety permit shall be executed immediately. If the party fails to comply with the penalty decision and does not file a prosecution within the time limit, the National Nuclear Safety Administration shall apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution.

Article 23 Any person who, by refusing to obey management, violating rules and regulations, or forcing others to work in violation of regulations and with risk, thereby causes a nuclear accident with serious consequences, which constitutes a crime, shall be investigated for criminal liability by the judicial authorities according to law.

Article 24 For the purpose of these Regulations, the following terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them:
(1) "Nuclear facility" means the various civil nuclear facilities listed in Article 2 of these Regulations.
(2) "Nuclear facility safety permit" means the written approval document issued by the National Nuclear Safety Administration for carrying out specific activities related to the nuclear facility, such as site selection and fixation, construction, commissioning, operation and decommissioning.
(3) "Operating entity" means the organization that applies for or holds a nuclear facility safety permit and may operate and run the nuclear facility.
(4) "Competent department of nuclear facilities" means the relevant administrative organ of the State Council or of the people's government of a province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government that bears leadership responsibility over the nuclear facility operating entity.
(5) "Nuclear accident" means an accident or series of accidents involving radioactivity, toxicity, explosivity or other hazards arising from nuclear fuel, radioactive products, waste within the nuclear facility or nuclear materials transported into or out of the nuclear facility.
Article 25 The National Nuclear Safety Administration shall formulate detailed implementation rules in accordance with these Regulations.
Article 26 These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
